results.outcome: Oxygenation (PaO2/FiO2) during PEEP titrated by transpulmonary pressure (Ptp, experimental) vs PEEP titrated by ARDSnet protocol (comparator). No primary outcome is named; the first physiological outcome reported in the abstract results is PaO2/FiO2 (the PEEP level itself was the first result mentioned but is the intervention dose delivered by the titration strategy, not a physiological outcome).
results.numerical_result: ARDS with IAH: 272±40 vs 209±50 mmHg, P=0.001; ARDS without IAH: 224±42 vs 214±45 mmHg, P=0.119 (Ptp vs ARDSnet). Abstract prints the IAH result as '(27.2±4.0) cmHg vs. (20.9± 5.0) cmHg' (unit mislabelled).
results.result_location: Table 3, p 3237 (gas exchange); Abstract Results, p 3234

1.1.support: A randomized, crossover study was conducted.
1.1.location: p 3236, Methods, Study design; Figure 2, p 3236

1.2.support: I looked for a description of how the allocation sequence was concealed until participants were enrolled and assigned (sealed opaque envelopes, central or remote randomization) and found none; the report states only that patients were randomized.
1.2.location: p 3236, Methods, Study design; Figure 2, p 3236

1.3.support: There were significantly differences in IAP, Pplat, Crs, Ccw, Cl and EELV between two groups at baseline. The other characteristics of ARDS patients in the two groups were well matched (Table 1).

S.1.support: The report does not state how many participants were allocated to each sequence order; Figure 2 shows a 'Randomized' step with arms for 'Ptp' and 'ARDSnet protocol' but no numbers per sequence.
S.1.location: p 3236, Methods, Study design and Figure 2

S.2.support: The difference of two groups was compared with the use of paired sample student's t test.

S.3.support: The report does not describe a washout period or the duration of the interval between the two ventilation phases (only a 'Baseline ventilation and measurement' step, Figure 2), so the time available for carryover effects to disappear before the second-period measurement cannot be judged.

2.1.support: Sedation was given with a continuous infusion midazolam (3 to 10 mg/h) and fentanyl (0.5 to 2.5 mg/h) to maintain a Ramsay score of 5-6 (no spontaneous breath) throughout the study and paralyzed with vecuronium if necessary.

2.2.support: PEEP levels and the FiO2 of each patient were titrated by Ptp and ARDSnet protocol. (The two strategies require different PEEP/FiO2 targets set at the bedside and no blinding of the clinical team is described.)

2.3.support: At each PEEP level (titrated by Ptp or ARDSnet protocol); patients were ventilated for 30 minutes to reach the equilibration of gas exchange and respiratory mechanics (Figure 2). (No protocol changes or trial-context-driven deviations are reported.)

2.4.support: Not applicable: question 2.3 was answered 'probably no' (no deviations from the intended intervention arising because of the trial context were reported), so the condition for this question is not met.

2.5.support: Not applicable: question 2.4 is 'NA' because its condition (Y/PY to 2.3) was not met, so this question is not answered.

2.6.support: The difference of two groups was compared with the use of paired sample student's t test. (All 15 randomized patients, 7 with and 8 without IAH, contributed measurements under both strategies.)

2.7.support: Not applicable: question 2.6 was answered 'yes' (a paired within-patient analysis of all randomized participants was used), so the condition for this question is not met.

3.1.support: Of 15 eligible ARDS patients receiving mechanical ventilation, seven ARDS patients with IAH and eight ARDS patients without IAH were included in the study (Figure 1 and Figure 2). All results tables report n=7 and n=8.

3.2.support: Not applicable: question 3.1 was answered 'yes' (outcome data were available for all randomized participants), so the condition for this question is not met.

4.2.support: All blood gas measurements were performed using an automated blood gas analyser. Measurements of variables were taken at baseline and 30 minutes after each ventilation phase.

4.3.support: PEEP levels and the FiO2 of each patient were titrated by Ptp and ARDSnet protocol. (The investigators applying the strategies and taking measurements were aware of which method was in use; no blinding is described.)

4.4.support: All blood gas measurements were performed using an automated blood gas analyser; PaO2/FiO2 is derived from objective laboratory values with FiO2 set by protocol-based scales, so knowledge of the intervention is unlikely to have influenced measurement of the outcome.
4.4.location: p 3235, Methods, Haemodynamics and blood gas analysis

4.5.support: Not applicable: question 4.4 was answered 'probably no' (the outcome is an automated laboratory measurement unlikely to be influenced by knowledge of the intervention), so the condition for this question is not met.

5.1.support: No protocol, trial registration record or statistical analysis plan is cited; the report states only that 'All analyses were performed using the SPSS 16.0 statistical package (SPSS Inc., Chicago, IL, USA)'.

5.2.support: I looked for evidence that only one of several eligible oxygenation measurements was reported; Table 3 reports PaO2/FiO2 together with pH, PaO2, SaO2, PaCO2 and A-aDO2 at the same time point for both subgroups, with no indication of result-based selection.

5.3.support: Analysis intentions are not available (no protocol or analysis plan is cited) and more than one eligible analysis of this crossover result exists (paired vs unpaired analysis, with or without period effects), so selection from among multiple analyses cannot be excluded.

5.4.support: The difference of two groups was compared with the use of paired sample student's t test. (Data from both periods contribute to the result, so the condition for this question is not met.)

D1.rationale: The study is described only as 'randomized'; neither the sequence generation (1.1 NI) nor any form of allocation concealment (1.2 NI) is reported, and the report does not explain how the order of the two ventilation strategies was assigned. No baseline imbalance suggesting a randomization problem was identified (1.3 N): the reported baseline differences are those produced deliberately by stratifying on intra-abdominal pressure, and each participant serves as their own control. The algorithm (NI in 1.1 and 1.2) gives Some concerns.

DS.rationale: The number of participants in each randomized sequence is not reported (S.1 NI), so period effects may not cancel; the analysis used only a paired t-test with no period or period-by-intervention term (S.2 PN); and the report gives no information on whether sufficient time elapsed between the two 30-minute ventilation phases for carryover effects (e.g. derecruitment after 17 cmH2O PEEP) to disappear before the second-period measurement (S.3 NI). Because the report does show a return to baseline ventilation between phases and does not demonstrate a carryover effect, I judge this domain Some concerns rather than High; the missing information about sequence balance, period effects and washout nevertheless lowers confidence in this result. A stricter reading of S.3 (no washout reported) could give High.

D2.rationale: Participants were deeply sedated (Ramsay 5-6) and could not be aware of the strategy (2.1 N), while the clinical team necessarily knew which titration method was in use (2.2 Y). No deviations from the intended intervention arising from the trial context are reported (2.3 PN); therefore 2.4 and 2.5 are not applicable. All randomized patients were analysed by a paired within-patient comparison of the two periods (2.6 Y). The algorithm gives Low risk of bias.

D3.rationale: Outcome data were reported for all 15 randomized participants (7 with IAH and 8 without IAH) in every results table, so 3.1 is Y and questions 3.2-3.4 are not applicable. The algorithm gives Low risk of bias.

D4.rationale: Oxygenation was measured with an automated blood gas analyser, an appropriate and objective method applied identically in both periods (4.1 N, 4.2 N). The outcome assessors were not blinded (4.3 Y), but knowledge of the intervention is unlikely to have influenced this automated laboratory measurement (4.4 PN), so 4.5 is not applicable. The algorithm gives Low risk of bias.

D5.rationale: There is no protocol, registry record or statistical analysis plan, so it cannot be confirmed that the data were analysed according to a pre-specified plan (5.1 NI), and for a crossover result with several eligible analyses (paired vs unpaired, with or without period effects) selection from among analyses cannot be excluded (5.3 NI). The reported measurements appear complete (5.2 PN) and both periods contribute to the result (5.4 N). The algorithm, with NI to 5.1, gives Some concerns.

overall.rationale: No domain is at high risk of bias, but three domains raise some concerns: the randomization process (sequence generation and concealment not reported), period/carryover effects (sequence balance, period effects and washout not reported) and selection of the reported result (no pre-specified analysis plan). These concerns rest mainly on missing information rather than demonstrated bias, so the overall judgement is Some concerns.
